title: Fiona the hippo: The Cincinnati Zoo’s famous resident is under medical observation after swallowing a hat | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Fiona the hippo, who became aninternational celebritywhen she was born at a record low weight and managed to survive against the odds, is under 24-hour monitoring after eating a knit cap that accidentally landed in her Cincinnati Zoo habitat, according to officials.

“We probably couldn’t make it happen again if we tried,” Cincinnati Zoo’s spokesperson said of the circumstance that led to Fiona ingesting the inedible object.

The knit cap was tossed into the air in front of the habitat and caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a 1-foot opening above the 12-foot-tall viewing windows, Communications Director Michelle Curley said.

The Cincinnati Zoo shared Tuesday that Fiona the hippo is receiving “24-hour care and attention.”

After ingesting the hat, the Cincinnati Zoo said Fiona received anti-nausea medication and laxative-like supplements to help “push things through” after eating it. This is because surgery isn’t an option for Fiona, which was confirmed after consulting both “veterinary and human specialists,” according to the Cincinnati Zoo.

“Our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she can pass it on her own,” a representative from the Cincinnati Zoo said Tuesday.

The Columbus Zoo donated a nine-foot scope and a technician to assist in giving a colonoscopy to Fiona. The colonoscopy showed Fiona’s intestines are bunching, which is a sign that something is passing through her small intestine, the update said.

For now, Fiona will continue to receive supportive care – including “all of her favorite foods” – and anti-nausea medication, the Cincinnati Zoo said.

The 9-year-old universally-loved ungulate is now being monitored by the zoo’s veterinary team and hippo care staff who are keeping her hydrated, according to the zoo.

“Her care team is cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self,” Cincinnati Zoo said in astatement.

Her caregivers are likely concerned the knit cap could cause an obstruction, according to Ron Magill, goodwill ambassador and conservation liaison for the Zoo Miami Foundation.

“The major concerns regarding Fiona ingesting a cap are primarily that it doesn’t cause an obstruction in her digestive tract which could lead to impaction and damage leading to serious infection and sepsis,” Magill told CNN.

Animals consuming items that accidentally fall into their habitats is not uncommon, according to Magill – and it’s not just hungry hippos that swallow them.

“Zoo Miami has had to surgically remove items such as a (collapsible) water bottle from a Komodo dragon and sunglasses from an alligator among many other things, including hearing aids and cell phones,” he said.

Fiona became asocial media darlingwhen she was born six weeks prematurely in 2017, weighing only 29 pounds at birth, CNN previously reported. Hippos are typically born closer to 100 pounds.

She became a big sister in 2022 when her mother, Bibi,gave birth to healthy boy, Fritz.

Fiona and her family are among the zoo’s top attractions, delighting guests by swimming in their habitat known as Hippo Cove and snacking on hippo-appropriate treats likewatermelonsand, most recently, awhole pumpkin.

Fiona even has her own line of merch at thezoo’s gift shop.

Now weighing around2,400 pounds, the princess of Hippo Cove faces a new challenge and will be kept out of public view while she being monitored, the Cincinnati Zoo said.

“Please help us keep our animals safe by securing your belongings and taking extra care near habitats,” the zoo said.

CNN’s Aidan Johnstone contributed to this report.

CNN’s Aidan Johnstone contributed to this report.
